subject.title: [Feature Request]: Native Prompt Caching Support for Amazon Nova (Bedrock)

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally move supported direct Amazon Bedrock Nova models from forced no-cache behavior to native cache-point eligible behavior after live proof is attached?
rationale: Source evidence proves the requested capability is missing, but enabling Nova caching changes default provider request shaping and billing behavior for existing users.

options.title: Land Nova caching after live proof
options.body: Require redacted Converse or ConverseStream proof and then accept the provider-owned cache policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

options.title: Require opt-in Nova caching
options.body: Keep forced no-cache as the upgrade default and allow Nova cache points only when users explicitly configure cacheRetention.

options.title: Defer Nova native caching
options.body: Leave the current no-cache behavior in place until maintainers are comfortable with the AWS contract and live provider evidence.

recommendation.title: Land Nova caching after live proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted Converse or ConverseStream proof and then accept the provider-owned cache policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent Bedrock provider and prompt-cache history makes this the strongest routing signal for the default-behavior decision.
